subject: ClariQ trial: evaluation playbook & shadowing plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <priya@clariq.com>; Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@clariq.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: ClariQ trial: evaluation playbook & shadowing plan

Hi Priyanka / Carlos —

Great sync today. Quick recap and proposed path for the trial so we can lock timelines and owners. I attached a short playbook and an initial rubric (see attachment stubs below). Please confirm or flag changes by EOD Wed so we can kick off next week.

What we heard (summary):
- Goal: reduce manual tagging latency for claims routing by 60% and keep precision > 92% for top-3 intents.
- Data: 200k historic claims, daily incoming ~3k. Sensitive fields to be redacted prior to test.
- Success window: 4-week trial with two phases (offline batch evaluation + live shadow).

Proposed trial plan (high level):
1) Week 0 (prep, 3 business days): ingest sample historic data (50k rows), agree on redaction pipeline and KPIs.
2) Week 1–2 (offline eval): run batched offline evals against the rubric, produce per-intent precision/recall and latency percentiles.
3) Week 3 (online shadow): 48–72 hour shadow run on a 10% traffic sample, measure end-to-end latency and mismatch rate vs. current system.
4) Week 4 (review): consolidation, scoring, and go/no-go decision.

Success criteria (draft):
- Accuracy: top-1 precision >= 92% OR top-3 recall >= 95% (weighted scoring in rubric).
- Latency: 95th percentile response < 220 ms in shadow environment.
- Stability: error rates < 0.5% and no systemic regressions vs historical baseline.

Ownership and next steps:
- Redwood: Jasmine (SE) — technical onboarding, infra and shadow setup. Aditya (AM) — contract/trial terms and billing guardrails.
- ClariQ: Carlos — integration owner; Priyanka — success criteria sign-off and business reviewer.

Attachments (stubs): clariq_trial_playbook_v1.pdf, clariq_eval_rubric.xlsx

If that matches, we will schedule a 30-minute kickoff on Monday to start data transfer and redaction checklist.

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Priyanka Rao <priya@clariq.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@clariq.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T17:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClariQ trial: evaluation playbook & shadowing plan

Thanks Marcus — this captures the call well. A few clarifications and requests from our side:

1) Data & redaction: we will send a 50k sample with PHI redacted by our ETL team. I attached our filled security questionnaire (security_questionnaire_clariq.pdf) — please have your security folks confirm the redaction checklist.

2) Evaluation preference: prefer a heavier weight on offline batch evaluation first (70% offline / 30% shadow) because we need deterministic reproducibility for procurement. We can do the short shadow later if offline scores look good.

3) Scoring tweak: suggest making latency a pass/fail at the trial stage rather than heavily weighted; business care more about accuracy on top-3 intents.

4) Timeline constraint: we cannot run shadow during our month-end close (Oct 26–29). If we go ahead, we prefer shadow in the week of Nov 9.

Carlos will be the integration lead; he will coordinate a VPN endpoint for secure transfers.

If you can adjust the rubric to 70/30 offline/online and make latency a gating check, we'll sign off to move forward.

— Priyanka
Director, Product Operations
ClariQ
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <priya@clariq.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@clariq.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClariQ trial: evaluation playbook & shadowing plan

Priyanka — thanks for the callout, that's totally reasonable. A few technical notes and concrete proposals from the SE side:

- Offline-first approach: we'll update the rubric to reflect 70% weight on offline batch metrics (per-intent precision/recall, confusion matrix, macro F1) and 30% on shadow results. I'll attach the updated worksheet before the kickoff.
- Latency gating: we'll treat latency as a gating criterion (pass/fail). For pass, 95p < 220ms. If latency fails but accuracy is met, we will propose a performance tuning cycle (quantization & batching adjustments) as a remediation path — not an immediate fail.
- Logs & telemetry: during offline runs we will provide tokenized model outputs + deterministic scoring scripts. For shadow, we'll capture request/response times and a mismatch report (redwood_shadow_mismatch.csv stub).
- Security: we can accept a pre-redacted sample over SFTP or an AWS presign link. For VPN, we can support an inbound SFTP endpoint behind our VPC.

Proposed kickoff agenda (30 min):
1) Quick intro and goals (5 min)
2) Data/ingest & redaction checklist (10 min)
3) Rubric walk-through and scoring mechanics (10 min)
4) Ops & timeline confirmations (5 min)

Related docs: https://drive.google.com/clariq/trial-playbook-v1 (playbook), https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/CLQ-2947 (deal record).

I'll block time Mon 10/19 10–10:30 PT for the kickoff unless you prefer earlier.

— Jasmine
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Rubric adjusted to 70% offline / 30% shadow (Jasmine to upload final rubric by Fri 10/16).
- Latency set as gating pass/fail (95p < 220ms). Jasmine will outline remediation steps in the rubric notes.
- Data transfer: Carlos to provide SFTP or presigned S3 link by 10/16. Redwood will verify redaction checklist within 24 hours of receipt.
- Kickoff scheduled: Mon 2026-10-19 10:00 PT (calendar invite coming).

Action items:
- Carlos: share transfer endpoint + contact for infra (due 2026-10-16).
- Priyanka: confirm sign-off on gating criteria (due 2026-10-16).
- Jasmine: upload updated rubric and offline scoring script (due 2026-10-16).

Attachments (stubs): clariq_trial_playbook_v1.pdf, clariq_eval_rubric.xlsx

If there are no objections, we'll proceed to the kickoff and data ingest next Monday.
